title: 洞仙歌·雪云散尽
title_en: Dong Xian Ge: The Snow Clouds Have Cleared
author: 李元膺

form.en: ci to the tune Dong Xian Ge, in two stanzas

text_note.zh: 资料库原文“颦”作“嚬”，“早”作“蚤”，都是古代的写法，意思一样，这里依通行写法。“池院”有的本子作“庭院”。
text_note.en: The source text writes pín (to frown) and zǎo (early) in older forms with the same meaning; this follows the usual modern forms. Some editions have 'courtyard' instead of 'pond and courtyard' in the second line.

readings.zh: “处”在这里是“地方”的意思，读 chù。
readings.en: Here the character means 'place', so it is read chù.

glosses.en: fàng xiǎo qíng: the sky clears at dawn.
chí yuàn: a courtyard with a pond.

glosses.zh: 青眼：正眼看人，表示喜欢。三国时阮籍对喜欢的人用黑眼珠正眼看，对讨厌的人翻白眼。柳树初生的嫩叶细长像眼睛，叫“柳眼”，所以说杨柳对人青眼相看。
glosses.en: qīng yǎn: looking at someone with dark eyes, that is, straight on, to show you like them. Ruan Ji of the Three Kingdoms looked straight at people he liked and showed the whites of his eyes to those he did not. New willow leaves are long and narrow like eyes, so the willows seem to look kindly at people.
fēng liú: charming and full of grace.

glosses.zh: 梅心：梅花的花心，指梅花。
glosses.en: méi xīn: the heart of a plum flower, meaning the plum blossom.

glosses.zh: 相映远：梅花和柳色远远地互相映衬。
glosses.en: xiāng yìng yuǎn: the plum and the willow set each other off from afar.

glosses.zh: 颦轻笑浅：轻轻皱眉，浅浅微笑。把初开的梅花和柳叶比作少女的神态。颦，皱眉。
glosses.en: pín qīng xiào qiǎn: a light frown, a faint smile. The new plum blossoms and willow leaves are pictured as a young girl's expressions. Pín means to frown.

glosses.zh: 浓芳：开得浓艳繁盛的花。
glosses.en: nóng fāng: flowers in full, rich bloom.

glosses.zh: 小艳疏香：小小的花朵，淡淡的香气，指早春的梅花。疏，稀少。
glosses.en: xiǎo yàn shū xiāng: small blossoms, faint scent, meaning the plum in early spring. Shū means sparse.

glosses.zh: 百紫千红：各种颜色的花开得满满的。
glosses.en: bǎi zǐ qiān hóng: flowers of every colour blooming everywhere.
sháo guāng: the lovely light of spring.
zhuī yóu: going out together to enjoy the sights.

glosses.zh: 醉红：喝醉后脸上泛起的红色。
glosses.en: zuì hóng: the flush on your face after drinking.

translation.en: The snow clouds have all cleared away,

translation.zh: 天亮时，有池塘的院子放晴了。
translation.en: and at dawn the pond and courtyard shine in clear weather.

translation.zh: 杨柳冒出嫩芽，好像用青眼看着人。
translation.en: The willows put out new leaves, as if looking kindly at people.

translation.zh: 和柳色远远地互相映衬，
translation.en: setting off the willows from afar,

translation.zh: 隐隐约约，像少女轻轻皱眉、浅浅微笑。
translation.en: faintly, like a girl's light frown and gentle smile.

translation.zh: 一年里春天最好的时候，
translation.en: The best part of the year's spring
is not when flowers bloom thick and rich,

translation.zh: 而是花小香淡的早春，最娇嫩柔美。
translation.en: but now, with small flowers and faint scent, softest and most delicate.

translation.zh: 万紫千红，花开得乱纷纷，
translation.en: flowers of every colour bloom in a riot,
and half the spring wind is already lost.

translation.zh: 要早早抢先占有这美好春光，
translation.en: So seize the lovely spring light early,
and go out together to enjoy it,
and never mind the spring chill:

translation.zh: 喝醉了脸上泛红，自然就暖和了。
translation.en: once the wine brings a flush to your face, you will be warm enough.

background.zh: 这首词前面有一段小序，大意是：一年的春景里，只有梅花和柳树刚发芽的时候意味最深。等到黄莺啼叫、百花烂漫，春天其实已经衰老了，让人没有新鲜感。所以作者写了这首《洞仙歌》，让去探春的人唱，免得错过了才后悔。词的意思和小序一样：要趁早春去赏春。
background.en: The poem has a short preface. It says that in all the spring scenery, the time when the plum blooms and the willows first bud means the most. By the time orioles sing and flowers are everywhere, spring is already old and feels stale. So the poet wrote this ci for spring-seekers to sing, so they would not regret coming too late. The ci says the same: go and enjoy spring while it is still early.

author_note.zh: 李元膺，北宋词人，生卒年不详，留下来的生平记载很少，一说是东平（今属山东）人，做过地方学官。他留下的词不多，这首《洞仙歌》因为见解新颖，被选进了《宋词三百首》。
author_note.en: Li Yuanying was a Northern Song ci poet. His dates are unknown and little is recorded about his life. One account says he came from Dongping, in today's Shandong, and served as a local school official. Few of his ci survive, but this one, with its fresh idea, was chosen for the famous anthology Three Hundred Song Ci.

appreciation.zh: 大多数人觉得百花齐放才是春天最美的时候，这首词偏偏唱反调。作者说，雪刚停、天刚晴，杨柳冒出细细的嫩芽，梅花开了一点点，像少女轻轻皱眉、浅浅一笑，这才最动人。等到清明，花开得满眼都是，春天已经过去一半了。这个道理很像生活：最美的东西常常在刚开始的时候，等你发现它“热闹”了，它也快结束了。最后几句很可爱：别怕春寒，喝点酒脸就红了，自己就暖和了，赶紧出去玩吧！
appreciation.en: Most people think spring is loveliest when every flower is out. This ci says the opposite. The poet says the best moment is when the snow has just stopped and the sky has just cleared, the willows show tiny new leaves, and a few plum blossoms open, like a girl's light frown or faint smile. By Qingming, when flowers fill your eyes, half of spring is already gone. It is a lot like life: the most beautiful part of a thing is often its beginning, and by the time it gets noisy and crowded it is nearly over. The last lines are playful. Don't worry about the chill. A little wine will flush your face and warm you up, so hurry out and enjoy it!
